title: Flip trigger timing, latch, and warmup cheatsheet
body:
brain dump + working checklist for flipping models (personal)

context:
- goal: safely flip small fractions of traffic to new model variant while minimizing spike risk and avoiding broad cache cold-starts.
- problem: large P95 spikes immediately after flip from KV cache thrash + tokenization edge cases (rare long tokens).
- this is my personal scratchpad for timing/latch heuristics and warmup techniques — experiment notes, not official playbook.

key ideas (short):
- latch window: enforce a minimum stable period (e.g., 30m) after any flip before another flip on same cohort — called "flip latch".
- timestamp-based backstop: if error-rate or latency spikes > threshold, start a lockout (e.g., 2h) during which no automatic flips occur.
- priming burst: run controlled synthetic warmup requests that mirror token-length distribution for the canary cohort immediately before flip.
- soft-pin TTL: pin clients to old variant but set TTL (e.g., 6h) so pins naturally expire to reduce long-term divergence.
- tokenization probe: run a small sample of client inputs through tokenizer pre-flip to detect rare tokenization blowups.

rollout flow (draft sequence):
1) preflight (T-60m):
   - run tokenizer-sample (1000 recent inputs sampled by auth hash) against new model variant to spot OOV/long-token rate.
   - run synthetic KV-warmup (50k tokens) targeting most-active cohorts. Use low-QPS traffic generator from infra/tools/warmup.
   - snapshot metrics: baseline P50/P95/P99, error_rate, 429/5xx split, median generation token length, avg KV cache hit rate.
2) prime window (T-10m -> T=0):
   - issue a 3-minute priming burst for cohort(s) that will receive traffic. Priming traffic should mimic client request size histogram.
   - verify memory/KV size stabilizes, no OOMs in serving nodes.
3) flip (T=0):
   - shift 0.5% traffic to variant A (hash-based cohort). Route rule: client_id % 10000 < 50.
   - start 15m tight watch window: 1m heartbeat checks for P95 and error spikes.
4) iterate: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% guided by metrics and time-of-day (avoid global peaks). Typical waits: 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h.
5) stable mark & lift: after 25% for 4h with no regression, remove soft-pin TTLs and allow normal rollout rules.

safety thresholds (initial heuristics):
- P95 increase > 25% absolute OR P95 exceeds 600ms -> rollback immediately.
- error_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points (absolute) -> pause and run deep-checks.
- sustained 429 increase -> check QPS throttles and error budget for the cohort, consider traffic shaping.
- any 5xx spike correlated to single host -> cordon host and continue (do not rollback entire variant immediately).

latch mechanics (notes):
- flip latch: after any automatic flip, block further automatic flips on that cohort for 30 minutes minimum.
- escalation latch: if P95 spike > 50% or error_rate +1pt, escalate to human (paging) and start 2h rollback lock.
- manual override path: SRE console button "force-unlatch" with required justification field + 2 approvers in audit log.

warmup details (practical):
- two warmup layers:
  1) tokenizer probe: run lightweight tokenization across 1k samples, record token counts distribution; fail flip if tail (>1% inputs) token_count > 4096.
  2) KV prime: for top-10 endpoints, replay last 1h of requests at 5x rate for 3 minutes to populate KV caches and JIT kernels. Avoid customer PII — use sanitized requests.
- priming should be run from same az/region as canary cohort to ensure cache locality.

client affinity + cohort hashing:
- prefer stable hashed cohorts by client_id over ephemeral session ids. Hash function: xxhash64(client_id) % 10000.
- record cohort -> variant mapping in flip log to allow retroactive debugging.

observability checklist (must have before flip):
- dashboards: per-cohort P50/P95/P99, error_rate, 429, 5xx, median token length, kv_hit_rate, model_inference_time, host_memory.
- distributed traces: capture 1-in-100 traces for post-flip deep dive; ensure span names include variant id.
- alerting hooks: temporary lowered thresholds for canary (e.g., P95 alert at 200ms lower than prod) to make regressions noisy.

post-flip followups (first 24h):
- record hourly summary in rollout diary (owner: me) for first 6h; then every 6h to 24h.
- compare top failure stack traces between old/new variant for signal of tokenization or decoding bugs.
- decide: continue ramp, hold and monitor, or rollback. If rollback, plan a primed reattempt after root cause addressed.

open questions / experiments to try:
- instead of synthetic warmup, can we replay warmup from a delayed stream of real requests (safer token distribution)? privacy/legal check needed.
- experiment with staggered priming across regions: priming in-region then global roll.
- automated TTL tuning for soft-pins based on cohort stability history (auto-extend for stable cohorts).

quick TODOs (me):
- [ ] add script that runs tokenizer-probe and outputs token tail percentiles (assign to Jinwoo)
- [ ] make a priming-job template in infra/warmup and test on staging (assign to Sofia)
- [ ] wire new pivot metric (kv_hit_rate) into canary dashboards (assign to me)
- [ ] write short doc for SRE on manual unlatch procedure + audit step (post-rollout)

notes-to-self:
- small flips at 02:00–05:00 UTC usually quieter for US-heavy traffic.
- keep flips on same day of week to compare weekday vs weekend behaviour.
- use conservative thresholds for first 3 flips, can relax after 25% sustained stability.

end of scratchpad. will refine after next flip attempt.
